themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendors have exploded in CD 210 this week with 6 complaints filed versus a historical average of 0.1 per week—a 4700% spike (z-score: 17.76)—signaling either a sudden influx of unlicensed operators or enforcement blind spots in Throgs Neck/Co-op City.
evidence: 6 mobile food vendor complaints filed this week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 17.76 indicates extreme statistical deviation from baseline
Concurrent spike in Vendor Enforcement complaints (5 last week vs. 0.2 avg, 1900% increase)
reporting_angles: Are unlicensed food vendors operating near schools, parks, or transit hubs in Co-op City?
Interview DSNY/DOH about why enforcement activity spiked and whether complaints preceded enforcement or vice versa

themes_detail.label: Facility Maintenance Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or Facility complaints surged to 36 this week, an 800% spike versus the 4.0 weekly average (z-score: 16.0), suggesting acute deterioration in public facility conditions across the district.
evidence: 36 maintenance/facility complaints filed this week vs. 4.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 16.0 indicates extreme statistical outlier
No recent local news or community board data clarifying which facilities are affected
reporting_angles: Which public facilities (parks, libraries, recreation centers, transit stations) are generating complaints?
Interview Parks Dept, DOE, and NYCHA (if applicable) to understand breakdown and remediation timeline

themes_detail.label: Noise Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Residential noise complaints jumped to 30 last week, a 224% increase versus the 9.2 weekly average (z-score: 5.2), indicating a sharp recent deterioration in quality of life across the district.
evidence: 30 noise complaints filed last week vs. 9.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (224% increase)
Z-score of 5.2 indicates significant statistical anomaly
Noise-Residential already a top-10 complaint category by volume (752 complaints over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Are complaints concentrated in specific neighborhoods (Throgs Neck vs. Co-op City) or building types (multi-family vs. single-family)?
Interview residents about noise sources (construction, bars, vehicles, events) and time-of-day patterns

themes_detail.label: Appliance Failure Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Appliance complaints nearly quadrupled to 13 last week, a 333% jump versus the 3.0 weekly average (z-score: 5.55), potentially indicating a building-wide or grid-related issue affecting heating/cooling systems.
evidence: 13 appliance complaints filed last week vs. 3.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (333% increase)
Z-score of 5.55 indicates significant statistical anomaly
Heat/Hot Water is already the second-largest complaint category (900 complaints over 90 days), suggesting chronic housing condition issues
reporting_angles: Are appliance failures concentrated in NYCHA buildings, rent-stabilized units, or across all building types?
Is there a utility outage, power surge, or grid instability affecting the district this week?

themes_detail.label: Encampment and Homelessness Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints spiked 700% to 3 complaints two weeks ago versus a 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.42), signaling emerging homelessness or street encampment activity in a traditionally lower-incidence area.
evidence: 3 encampment complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% increase)
Z-score of 5.42 indicates significant statistical anomaly for this complaint type
Long-standing CB budget requests for social services (home-delivered meals, aging services) suggest underlying unmet demand
reporting_angles: Where are encampments clustering (parks, transit areas, parking lots) and what services are nearby?
Interview homeless outreach teams and social services providers about whether Co-op City/Throgs Neck is seeing increased demand
